claims.text: Partial substitution of Mn with a small amount of Ti will improve the mechanical performance of MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration material.
Ti-substituted MnNiSi will retain a large magnetocaloric effect.
Ti substitutes for Mn in the MnNiSi lattice.
Ti substitution modifies the lattice structure and bonding characteristics.
The lattice and bonding modifications caused by Ti enhance ductility and reduce brittleness.
Ti substitution alters the electronic structure and bonding environment of the MnNiSi lattice.
The altered electronic structure and bonding environment may reduce internal stresses.
Reduced internal stresses improve the mechanical properties of the material.
Small Ti substitutions do not significantly disrupt the magnetic ordering responsible for the magnetocaloric effect.
Ti-substituted samples will have higher fracture toughness or lower brittleness than Ti-free MnNiSi.
The magnetocaloric effect after Ti substitution will remain within 90–95% of the Ti-free baseline value.
The proposed effects are expected at room temperature and during cyclic magnetic-field exposure relevant to magnetic refrigeration.
The hypothesis is expected to hold for Ti substitution levels below 10 atomic percent.
Higher Ti substitution levels may significantly degrade the magnetocaloric effect.
The mechanical and magnetocaloric effects of Ti substitution are uncertain because no direct eligible evidence is cited.
Failure to improve mechanical performance, or a magnetocaloric effect below 90% of baseline at any tested substitution level, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The stated applicability range is below 10 atomic percent Ti, but the experiment includes a 10% sample and the rule says failure at any tested level falsifies the hypothesis. Thus an outcome at a composition outside the stated boundary could incorrectly be treated as decisive.
